target.title: fix(clawhub): validate content-length with parseMediaContentLength
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`src/infra/clawhub.ts` uses `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` to parse the Content-Length response header — the same pattern that was replaced in `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts` by #105954. Unlike `parseMediaContentLength` (from `@openclaw/media-core/content-length`), `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` does not validate comma-separated or duplicate Content-Length values, nor does it reject values outside `Number.isSafeInteger`. A malformed header passes through as a parsed number instead of being rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt `parseMediaContentLength`, the same shared helper that #105954 already validated for camera downloads. This is the only remaining `src/` call site that parses a Content-Length header with `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger`.

## User Impact

Malformed Content-Length headers from ClawHub responses are now rejected with a clear error. Valid headers are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/infra/clawhub.ts` — replaced `parseStrictNonNegativeInteger` with `parseMediaContentLength`; adjusted `undefined` check to `null`
- `packages/media-core/src/content-length.test.ts` — existing tests for the helper
- `pnpm test src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — 69 passed, 0 regressions

target.title: fix(agents): keep read warning args previews UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `read` tool validation warning preview must be both UTF-16 safe and visibly truncated when raw string args exceed the warning preview budget. The first safe-slice fix avoided split surrogate output, but at an emoji boundary it could shrink the raw prefix to exactly the final preview limit and accidentally drop the existing ellipsis marker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The follow-up keeps an explicit `wasRawTruncated` signal before sanitization. If the raw args exceeded the warning preview budget and the sanitized safe prefix did not already include the truncation marker, the warning preview appends the existing ellipsis marker while still avoiding lone surrogate output.

## User Impact

Read-tool validation warnings and console diagnostics stay well-formed at emoji/astral boundaries and still visibly indicate that oversized args were truncated.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head after bot follow-up: `1e6f0ab0fa0`
- `git diff --check`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`: pass
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts`: pass
- Production-handler proof with `node --import tsx --input-type=module` calling `handleToolExecutionStart` for `read` args shaped as `200 x chars + U+1F600 + tail`:

```json
{
  "event": "embedded_read_tool_start_warning",
  "codePoints": 201,
  "lastCodePointHex": "2026",
  "ellipsisPreserved": true,
  "containsEmoji": false,
  "loneSurrogate": false,
  "consoleMessageTail": "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx?"
}
```

- Regression coverage now expects both oversized ASCII args and the emoji-boundary args path to retain the truncation marker without producing lone surrogates.

Known proof gap: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts -- --testNamePattern "read warning args"` did not return output before the local 180s timeout in this Windows worktree, so the current update does not claim a fresh local Vitest pass. CI should provide the full test signal for the pushed head.
